text:
The Kings arrive at Nassau Coliseum off a 5-2 win at WSH, their first in a six-game winless run (0-4-2), after coming back from two goals down. They're 1-3-1 in their last five and were outscored 14-9 in it, and they're missing Alex Turcotte. The Islanders are 3-1-1 over the same stretch after a 3-2 home win over ANA, but they're without Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie. Simon Holmstrom (now 20:11 a night, up from 15:43) and Kyle Palmieri (19:14, up from 15:38) are absorbing those minutes.

The numbers say these teams are close. At five on five, LAK has taken 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and NYI 53%. Our model has LAK at 3.0 expected goals tonight and NYI at 2.89. NYI's results run ahead of their chances, with goaltending doing the lifting, while LAK has been better than its record. LAK also takes 4.6 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays.

In net, projected starter Darcy Kuemper is at -2.6 goals saved above expected this season (-6.8 last year), while projected Semyon Varlamov, in for Ilya Sorokin, is at +3.4.

Watch Adrian Kempe (38% to score, top power play) and Artemi Panarin (34%, due) for LAK, and Bo Horvat (41%, top power play) for NYI. Our under-the-radar pick is Scott Laughton, a third-liner with 1.5 expected goals over his last seven games, including four high-danger shots.
